finding.title: Give streakAlertSyncEffect the same cold-start defense and test coverage as reminderSyncEffect

evidence.quote:
// M3 fix: the pref notifiers return defaults (enabled=true, 19:00)
  // synchronously, then async-load the real values.

final enabled = ref.watch(streakAlertEnabledProvider);
  final time = ref.watch(streakAlertTimeProvider);

finding.why: reminderSyncEffect was patched (M3) specifically because trusting the raw preference-provider state schedules with transient defaults first; streakAlertSyncEffect, structurally identical and in the same file, still watches streakAlertEnabledProvider/streakAlertTimeProvider directly and inherits the same defect. No test in the notifications suite drives streakAlertSyncEffectProvider's real body -- every reference to it anywhere in the repo's notifications tests stubs it to `(ref) async {}` -- so a regression that schedules/cancels a streak alert against the user's actual saved preference during a cold-start or profile-switch window would go undetected.
finding.recommendation: Apply the same direct-SharedPreferences-read pattern reminderSyncEffect uses (or fix at the root per the SM-2 finding), and add a streak_alert_cold_start_test.dart mirroring reminder_sync_sacred_time_test.dart's recording-gateway approach.
acceptance_criteria: A new test with a recording NotificationGateway/StreakAlertService fake asserts streakAlertSyncEffect does not schedule/cancel using default streak-alert settings when the persisted value differs, mirroring reminder_sync_sacred_time_test.dart.

finding.title: Delete the dead pre-per-profile notification scheduling API in NotificationGateway/NotificationScheduler
finding.why: WS5.per-profile replaced these with *ForProfile equivalents (per the 'H1 fix' comments elsewhere in the file); a repo-wide grep for non-declaration, non-test callers of all 9 methods returns nothing, confirming zero production callers. Yet they still compile and are still exercised by roughly 780 of notification_gateway_test.dart's 1415 lines plus the entirety of notification_scheduler_test.dart and notification_service_test.dart. A future edit that calls scheduler.schedule()/.cancel() instead of the *ForProfile variant -- same class, plausible-looking name -- would silently reintroduce H1 (two competing ID schemes per profile) with no compiler or test signal, since the dead path still 'works' and stays green in CI.
finding.recommendation: Delete the 9 legacy methods and the singleton ID constants, delete/collapse the corresponding dead tests, and keep only the *ForProfile surface.
acceptance_criteria: grep -rn for the 9 legacy method names in lib/ returns zero results once removed.
notification_gateway_test.dart / notification_scheduler_test.dart / notification_service_test.dart shrink accordingly with no loss of coverage on the *ForProfile paths.

finding.title: Wire up or delete the unused SharedPrefsNotificationPreferencesRepository

evidence.quote:
/// All key strings and default values are centralised here rather than
/// being scattered across multiple Riverpod notifiers.

finding.why: SharedPrefsNotificationPreferencesRepository is constructed nowhere in lib/ outside its own constructor declaration -- a repo-wide grep confirms zero call sites. Its doc comment claims prefs are centralised here instead of being scattered across notifiers, but every one of the 5 preference providers in notification_providers.dart still reads/writes SharedPreferences key-by-key inline via the static key helpers, exactly the scattered pattern the class claims to replace. It has zero test coverage and misleads a reader into believing there is a repository DI seam here when there isn't one.
finding.recommendation: Either finish the migration (route the 5 providers' load/save through a provider constructing this repository) or delete the class and the interface's now-pointless abstract load()/save(), keeping only the static key helpers that are actually used.
acceptance_criteria: Either a provider constructs SharedPrefsNotificationPreferencesRepository and the 5 notifiers call load()/save() through it with a test exercising both methods; or the class and abstract methods are removed and dart analyze stays clean.

finding.title: Route sacred_window_repository.dart through the sacred_time barrel instead of deep cross-feature imports (Rule 2)

evidence.quote: match($1, /features\/([^\/]+)\//, a); match($0, /features\/([^\/]+)\//, b); if(a[1] != b[1]) print

finding.why: features/notifications reaches directly into features/sacred_time's domain internals instead of features/sacred_time/sacred_time.dart (itself an empty stub barrel with no exports), so a refactor inside sacred_time's domain layer can silently break notification scheduling with no barrel-boundary warning. Separately, make audit check 15's awk pattern always compares a feature name against itself: it runs match() against $0 (the whole grep -rn line, which starts with the FILE PATH), so the first 'features/X/' match in $0 is always the same X captured from $1 -- a[1] and b[1] can never differ, so check 15 can never print a warning for ANY file. This is confirmed empirically: check 15 produced zero WARN output in the clean-tree baseline despite this real cross-feature import existing.
finding.recommendation: Populate features/sacred_time/sacred_time.dart with the needed exports (SacredLocation, SacredWindow, ZmanimWindowService) and import through it; separately fix the Makefile check 15 awk pattern to extract the import path (not the full grep line) before comparing feature names.
acceptance_criteria: make audit check 15, once its awk bug is fixed, flags this file today and reports clean after the barrel fix is applied.

finding.title: Wrap SacredWindowEntries clear+insert in one transaction (DB-2)
finding.why: The table is briefly empty between clearAll() completing and insertAll() starting; neither call is awaited by any caller and neither is wrapped in a transaction. invalidate()'s own separate unawaited clearAll() (line 50) can also interleave with _persistToDb()'s clear-then-insert pair (line 167) in either order. The class's own doc says this cache exists so 'background notification-fire-time checks can read them on cold-start without the Flutter engine' -- a background read landing in the empty gap, or after invalidate() wins a race against a slower insertAll(), sees no Sacred Time windows and could fail to suppress a notification during Shabbos/Yom Tov, the entire point of DNI-367. Confirming the full consequence requires reading the background notification-fire-time isolate handler, which is outside this batch.
finding.recommendation: Wrap clear+insert in one db.transaction(...) and await it from both invalidate() and _persistToDb(), or add an explicit generation-counter guard so a stale clear can't stomp a newer insert.
acceptance_criteria: A DAO-level test that races invalidate() against a concurrent _persistToDb() cycle never observes SacredWindowEntries transition through an empty state once a non-empty write has committed.
